en: Mount Mayon in Albay is widely recognized for its nearly perfect conical shape among all active volcanoes in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley into the Babuyan Channel.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the second-largest lake in the Philippines and the largest lake on the island of Mindanao.
The Philippine eagle is the national bird of the Philippines and is critically endangered, primarily inhabiting the tropical forests of Mindanao.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Mount Apo, located in Mindanao, is the highest mountain in the Philippines with an elevation of approximately 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its rich marine biodiversity.
Baguio City in Benguet province is known as the Summer Capital of the Philippines because of its cool mountain climate.
Samar is the third-largest island in the Philippines and is geographically separated from Leyte by the narrow San Juanico Strait.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is a complex volcano featuring a main crater lake on Volcano Island within the larger Taal Lake.
The tamaraw, a small, V-horned buffalo, is an endangered species endemic to the island of Mindoro in the Philippines.
